required_context_phrases: linearization about a homogeneous steady state
fixed domain without growth or mechanics
domain large compared with the wavelength

primary_source.citation: A. M. Turing (1952) The chemical basis of morphogenesis, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. B 237(641):37-72, doi:10.1098/rstb.1952.0012
primary_source.read_copy: https://www.dna.caltech.edu/courses/cs191/paperscs191/turing.pdf (37-page JSTOR scan, fetched 2026-10-31; not redistributed here)
primary_source.passage_used: Section 'Types of asymptotic behaviour in the ring after a lapse of time' (printed pp. ~51-53): on a ring the wave-lengths 'must be submultiples of the' circumference; the 'chemical wave-length' is 'achieved whenever possible' but a finite ring must 'make do' with a wavelength that divides it exactly.
primary_source.scope_note: Turing's finite-domain discussion is a ring (periodic) of cells/continuous tissue; this adapter uses a 1-D interval with zero-flux (Neumann) ends, which is an ADAPTER-ADDED domain choice using standard separation of variables, not a statement Turing makes.
